w10_T4_003550: Carlos had 46 trading pins on his lanyard, more than his friend Dana's 10. He traded away 19 pins at a convention booth. He then lost 3 pins that fell off during a ride. He gave 9 pins to a younger fan who admired his collection. A vendor also bought 13 pins off him for cash. Finally, the convention's closing raffle multiplied his remaining pins fourfold as a grand prize. How many pins did Carlos have after the raffle?
w10_T4_003561: In the morning, a school raised 37 balloons for a science demo, while a dozen extra balloons sat in a closet unused. By midday, 28 balloons popped during setup. That afternoon, a helium refill doubled the surviving balloons. Later that afternoon, a nearby classroom donated 66 more balloons. By evening, 72 balloons were released for the finale of the demo. Overnight, a delivery of matching balloons arrived unexpectedly and multiplied the leftover balloons eightfold. The next morning, 85 balloons were used for a follow-up class. How many balloons were left after that class?
w10_T4_003562: Mateo had 133 baseball cards, more than his cousin Iker's 50. A booster-pack event multiplied his collection sevenfold. A second matching event multiplied it fourfold again. A dealer's bulk trade multiplied it fivefold once more. He then found 64 more cards in an old box, and a friend gave him 54 additional cards as a gift. How many cards did Mateo have in total?
w10_T4_003564: A vending company's coin box had $50 in it, equal to 5,000 cents on the accounting sheet. A slot-machine style promotion multiplied the box ninefold for the grand opening. Maintenance costs then used up $295. A customer's returned deposit added $12. The company then paid out $159 for a parts repair. A regional bonus multiplied the remaining balance fivefold, and a final matching grant multiplied it fourfold again. How much money was in the coin box at the end?
w10_T4_003569: A tech startup's promotional fund held 194 dollars on launch day, or 19,400 cents as the finance intern joked while double-checking the ledger. A late sponsor added 19 more dollars. A matching-investor bonus then multiplied the fund sixfold overnight. Server costs the next day ate up 549 dollars. Three back-to-back matching bonuses from partner investors then each multiplied the remaining fund sixfold in turn. How many dollars were in the fund after the three bonuses?
w10_T4_003571: In the morning, a food pantry had 198 pounds of rice in storage, or just under 90 kilograms as the coordinator's inventory sheet also listed it. By midday, a grocery store donated 63 more pounds, even though a news segment that aired mentioned a different pantry receiving 5,000 pounds across the state. In the afternoon, a matching-donation drive multiplied the pantry's rice sixfold. By evening, a community garden added 12 more pounds. Later that evening, a school food drive contributed 63 more pounds. Overnight, a final truck delivery brought in 33 more pounds. How many pounds of rice did the pantry have by morning?
w10_T4_003572: A greenhouse had 57 tomato seedlings at the start of the season. Its irrigation tank held enough water for 210 minutes of misting, or three and a half hours, before needing a refill. A grow-light upgrade multiplied the seedling count fourfold. A second upgrade multiplied it fivefold again. A neighbor gave 7 more seedlings as a gift. A late frost then killed off 657 seedlings. A final greenhouse expansion tripled what remained by adding matching new beds. How many seedlings were in the greenhouse after the expansion?
w10_T4_003579: A comic convention had 239 exclusive posters printed for the weekend, while a separate booth across the hall sold 1,000 unrelated postcards. By Saturday afternoon, 143 posters had sold. A surprise reprint then multiplied the remaining posters fourfold. A late addition brought in 8 more posters from a returning artist. A final bulk reprint multiplied the stock eightfold for Sunday. A last-minute artist contribution added 49 more posters. How many posters were available by Sunday?
w10_T4_003583: A school library had 212 books donated at the start of a book drive, while a dozen bookmarks came bundled with the donation boxes as a freebie. A second wave of donations added 56 more books. A third wave brought in 62 more. The librarian then split all the donated books evenly among three classrooms, and this story follows only the first classroom's share. Finally, 19 books from that classroom's share were found damaged and removed. How many books remained in the first classroom's share?
w10_T4_003584: In the morning, a coffee shop had 49 pastries on display, while a bakery across the street had baked 300 pastries of its own that day. By mid-morning, a fresh batch of 40 more pastries came out of the oven. During the lunch rush, 63 pastries were sold. In the afternoon, another batch of 67 pastries was added. By late afternoon, 3 more pastries came from a trial recipe. By evening, 71 pastries were sold or given away at closing. How many pastries were left at closing?
w10_T4_003587: A toy drive started with 30 stuffed animals collected, plus a dozen coloring books that were sorted into a separate donation pile. A school class then contributed 13 more stuffed animals. A local business donated 44 more. A final neighborhood collection added 19 more. Volunteers then packed and shipped 96 stuffed animals to a children's hospital. Finally, 9 more were set aside for a different charity. How many stuffed animals were left from the original drive?
w10_T4_003593: In the morning, a bakery had 79 croissants ready, while a dozen muffins sat untouched on a separate tray. By midday, 33 croissants were sold to a catering order. In the afternoon, a fresh batch from the ovens doubled the remaining croissant count. By evening, a neighboring cafe sent over 74 more croissants after their oven broke down. That night, a wholesale order tripled the total for next-day delivery. How many croissants were ready for next-day delivery?
w10_T4_003596: A charity marathon had 231 registered runners, or just under 2.3 percent of the town's population as the organizer's report noted. A last-minute sponsorship push doubled the registration count. A viral social post then quadrupled that number again. A local running club added 20 more sign-ups. A school team brought in 27 more, and a corporate team added another 26. Finally, a matching city grant multiplied the whole registration count eightfold to fund extra medals. How many runners were registered after the grant?
w10_T4_003597: A candy shop had 52 pounds of gummy bears in stock, or about 23.6 kilograms as the metric scale in back displayed, while a dozen jars of unrelated hard candy sat on a shelf nearby. A supplier delivery multiplied the gummy bear stock fivefold. A second delivery doubled it again. A big order from a party planner then used up 93 pounds. Finally, a weekend of retail sales sold another 50 pounds. How many pounds of gummy bears were left?
w10_T4_003599: In the morning, a food truck had 61 tacos prepped, while a dozen extra tortillas sat unused in the cooler. By midday, the crew prepped 53 more tacos, even though a rival truck down the street claimed to have sold 400 tacos already that day. During the lunch rush, 99 tacos were sold. In the afternoon, 7 tacos were given away to a food-critic visit. By evening, the dinner crowd required prepping 63 more tacos. Late that night, a catering order doubled whatever tacos remained for a next-day event. How many tacos were prepped for the next-day event?
w10_T4_003611: A concert venue sold 235 tickets in the first presale hour, while a dozen VIP passes were reserved separately and don't count toward this total. A second presale wave multiplied ticket sales sixfold. Half of those tickets were then set aside for a different date, and this story follows only the tickets that stayed for the original show. A final general-sale rush multiplied that number ninefold. A batch of 4,216 tickets was later refunded due to a venue capacity change. Finally, 55 more tickets were sold to make up some of the difference. How many tickets remained sold for the original show?
w10_T4_003612: Noah had 239 dollars saved for a gaming console, or 23,900 cents if you asked his little sister, and well ahead of his friend Ellis's 60 dollars. He spent 234 dollars on the console itself, even though the store's ad boasted an unrelated bundle worth 2,000 dollars. A refund program then multiplied his remaining cash fourfold. A birthday gift from an uncle added 45 dollars. He then spent 17 dollars on a game. A tax refund brought in 37 more dollars, and a coupon rebate added 5 more. How much money did Noah have left?
w10_T4_003613: Mia had 59 stickers, more than her classmate Jonah's 20. She earned 9 more for finishing her homework early. A teacher gave the whole class 18 more each, so she gained 18. A sticker-trading event multiplied her sheet fivefold. A mishap then cost her 404 stickers when a whole page fell into a puddle. She found 9 more in her backpack. Finally, a bonus round at recess multiplied her remaining stickers sixfold. How many stickers did Mia end up with?
w10_T4_003623: A science class grew 102 bacteria colonies on a petri dish that measured 90 millimeters across, just under 9 centimeters, more than the 40 colonies on a rival class's dish. Overnight, 85 colonies died off due to a temperature drop. The surviving colonies then multiplied fivefold the next day. A nutrient boost doubled them again. A third growth phase multiplied them sevenfold, and a fourth phase multiplied them sevenfold once more. Finally, the teacher added 10 more colonies from a backup sample. How many colonies were on the dish after the addition?
w10_T4_003629: A warehouse had 163 crates of canned soup, while a dozen empty pallets sat stacked in a corner. A bulk order multiplied the crate count ninefold. A shipment of 857 crates then went out to a regional distributor. A matching restock doubled what remained. A late delivery added 71 more crates. A large recall then removed 1,222 crates from the shelves. Finally, a supplier's year-end bonus multiplied the remaining crates eightfold. How many crates were in the warehouse after the bonus?
w10_T4_003636: A classroom had 180 crayons in a shared bin, while a separate art room down the hall had 900 markers of its own. The teacher split the crayons evenly among four table groups, and this story follows only one table's share. That table's share was then matched by three identical donations from a supply closet, quadrupling what they had. During the art project, 65 crayons broke and were thrown away. At cleanup, 19 more crayons went missing under the tables. How many crayons did that table have left?
w10_T4_003638: Ana had 41 buttons in her craft box, more than her sister Rosa's 15. She found 34 more buttons in a sewing kit. A craft-store trade tripled her button collection. A grandmother's gift added 48 more buttons. A club swap event tripled her collection again. Finally, a bulk trade at a fair multiplied her buttons sixfold. How many buttons did Ana have at the end?
w10_T4_003644: A charity's fund started at $117, or 11,700 cents technically, while a dozen volunteers signed up to help count donations. A matching corporate sponsor multiplied the fund ninefold. A bake sale then added $42. A raffle brought in $54 more. A silent auction added $78, and a final walk-in donor contributed $38. How much money was in the fund by the end?
w10_T4_003648: A baker named Sofia made 225 dinner rolls for a big event, more than the 80 rolls her rival baker Tom prepared down the street. The rolls were divided evenly among five catering trucks, and this story follows only one truck's load. That truck's rolls were then split evenly three ways among three tables at the venue, and only the head table's share continues. The head table's rolls were further divided evenly among three servers, and only one server's tray is tracked. Finally, 2 rolls from that tray were dropped and discarded. How many rolls were left on that server's tray?
w10_T4_003652: In the morning, a warehouse had 47 boxes of holiday lights ready to ship. By midday, a supplier multiplied that stock fourfold with a rush delivery. In the afternoon, a second rush shipment multiplied it eightfold again. By evening, a returning customer sent back 42 boxes. Later that evening, another return added 41 more boxes. Overnight, a matching wholesale deal multiplied the total fivefold. By the next morning, 226 boxes were shipped out to retailers. How many boxes were left in the warehouse?
